literal: That which was seen was indeed only one day; the public rumor indeed is like the snake seizing the moon.
translation: Our meeting was but for a single day; yet the public gossip about it has spread instantly, like the eclipse of the moon seized by the serpent.
modern: நாங்கள் ஒருவரை ஒருவர் பார்த்தது ஒரு நாள் மட்டுமே; ஆனால் எங்களைப் பற்றிய வதந்தி, பாம்பானது சந்திரனைப் பிடித்துக் கொண்ட கிரகணத்தைப் போல எங்கும் பரவிவிட்டது.
explanation: The heroine laments how quickly and widely the town has begun to gossip about her secret love. She points out that she and her lover met for only a single day ('கண்டது ஒருநாள்'). Yet, the resulting public rumor ('அலர்') has spread instantly to everyone, just like a lunar eclipse ('திங்களைப் பாம்புகொண்டற்று') where a serpent is believed to seize the moon, drawing the attention of the entire world. The contrast between the brief, private meeting and the massive, public gossip highlights her distress.
